audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer labels the matchup FAV while giving it a difficulty of 8/10, and the level chart hands Heimerdinger five of seven stages. Three signals, three different verdicts.
audit.why: The page's own table has Sejuani at 52.63% over 133 games. A win rate two and a half points above even does not support an 8/10 difficulty, and an 8/10 difficulty does not support a FAV label. Difficulty and diff are both writable, but changing either one silently would move the site's rating for a lane on a judgement call rather than a fact.
audit.corrected: Nothing changed. The prose was made mechanical without touching diff, diffRating or the chart. Recorded in questionsForUser.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid block claims his empowered rockets 'chunk you for 15-20% HP every rotation'.
audit.why: No percentage like that exists anywhere in the kit data, and Riot's text for Hextech Micro-Rockets and UPGRADE!!! gives no health-scaling component at all. A specific number a player will trust should not be invented. The real spike numbers are Micro-Rockets at 1325 range on 11/10/9/8/7s and UPGRADE!!! at 100/85/70s.
audit.corrected: The invented percentage removed and replaced with the range and cooldown that make the poke actually oppressive.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two systematic errors. (a) 'your Permafrost armor passive', 'your passive Permafrost armor', 'your Permafrost armor passive stacks so fast' — five occurrences fusing Permafrost with Fury of the North's Frost Armor and inventing a stack mechanic. (b) Glacial Prison is called a root three times ('root him in place', 'root him in open space').
audit.why: Riot on Fury of the North: 'After being out of combat, Sejuani gains Frost Armor which grants Armor and Magic Resist and immunity to slows.' No stacks, and no connection to Permafrost, which is a 1.5s stun that fires at maximum Frost stacks. Riot on Glacial Prison: it 'freezes and stuns the first champion hit' — a stun, not a root. The distinction matters here because a stun stops him casting a turret or a grenade, which is precisely why the level-6 play works.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor named correctly throughout; stun replaces root.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names 'CH-2 Grenade (Stun)' as matchup-defining with no number, and pads with a generic 'Q dash spent on poke' line.
audit.why: CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade is 11 seconds flat at every rank, 970 range, and Riot specifies that it stuns 'anyone directly hit' while merely slowing those around them — so a partial hit costs you far less than a direct one. Micro-Rockets are 11/10/9/8/7s at 1325. The turret itself is a 1-second charge-based cooldown, which is why turrets cannot be tracked as a window.
audit.corrected: The 11 seconds and the direct-hit-versus-splash distinction written into the cooldown block, report[5] and loading.

audit.why: The page's jungle framing is right and worth keeping: Heimerdinger has no dash and no escape in Riot's kit, so a landed Glacial Prison plus any jungler equals a kill. That is the one lever that flips this lane and it is already stated.

edits.after: At level 1 you have real agency: Heimer has no turrets down yet and Frost Armor from Fury of the North soaks his rockets. Walk up, auto twice to start stacking Frost, and the moment he repositions to place his first turret, Arctic Assault into Winter's Wrath's second swing applies a full Frost stack — Permafrost then stuns, and you have first-blood pressure before his nest exists. Level 2 gives the same window, shrinking: get the Q knock-up trade in before his second turret materialises or the lane shifts. Level 3 is genuinely contested — his turrets are nearly full and CH-2 Electron Storm Grenade is live at 11 seconds — but your Q-W-E chain still bursts him if you catch him away from turret coverage.
edits.before: At level 1 you have real agency: Heimer has no turrets down yet and your passive Permafrost armor soaks his W rocket. Walk up, auto-attack twice to start stacking Frost, and the moment he repositions to place his first turret, Arctic Assault into Winter's Wrath's second swing applies a full Frost stack — Permafrost stun and you have first blood pressure before his nest exists. Level 2 gives you the same window but shrinking: get the Q knock-up trade in before his second turret materialises or the lane shifts against you. Level 3 is genuinely contested — his turrets are nearly full and his grenade E is live, but your own Q-W-E chain can burst him if you catch him standing in a bad spot away from turret coverage.

edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are his lane. Three H-28 G turrets zone the entire wave, Hextech Micro-Rockets poke from 1325 every 11 seconds, and your Arctic Assault path runs straight through the beams. Do not charge in. Farm only with Winter's Wrath at maximum range, let Frost Armor absorb what poke you cannot dodge, and use Doran's Shield to stay relevant. At level 6 his UPGRADE!!! turrets make diving suicidal — but Glacial Prison changes the equation: throw it from 1300 to catch him stepping forward to place a turret or to poke, stun him in open ground, then close with Q and chain Permafrost before the nest can save him. He has no dash and no escape, so the stun is the whole play.
edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are his lane. At level 6 his UPGRADE!!! ult-empowered turrets make diving suicidal — but your Glacial Prison changes the equation: throw it long-range to catch him stepping forward to place a new turret or walk up to poke, root him in open space, then close with Q and chain the Permafrost stun before his nest can save him.

edits.after: First-item Sunfire Aegis flips your durability profile: Immolate deals constant damage on contact and its resistances let you absorb enough rocket poke to actually reach him, which makes the Q-R-E chain reliably lethal in a short corridor. At 2+ items you are unkillable in a straight duel — the moment Heimer steps past his nest with CH-2 Grenade on its 11 seconds, Glacial Prison into Arctic Assault into Permafrost is a guaranteed kill. In teamfights throw R into the backline rather than the turret cluster; if he re-deploys turrets mid-fight, Arctic Assault through them to reach him, because his kit has zero mobility and no answer to sustained in-your-face CC.
edits.before: First-item Sunfire Aegis flips your durability profile: its Immolate aura deals consistent damage on contact and its armor/MR let you absorb enough rocket poke to actually reach him, making your Q-R-E CC chain reliably lethal in a short corridor. notes: Removed a fabricated statistic: the mid block claimed his empowered rockets 'chunk you for 15-20% HP every rotation'. Nothing in the kit data supports a percentage, and a number that specific is exactly the kind of thing a player will plan around. A genuinely useful distinction was missing and has been added: Riot's grenade text stuns 'anyone directly hit' and only slows the surrounding area, so clipping the edge of CH-2 is survivable and eating the centre is not. Also fixed five occurrences of 'Permafrost armor passive' (it is Frost Armor from Fury of the North, an out-of-combat buff, and it does not stack) and three calls of Glacial Prison a 'root' when Riot's text says it stuns the first champion hit. RATING CONFLICT left untouched and escalated: this page carries diff FAV, diffRating 8/10, and a level chart giving Heimerdinger five of seven stages, against a 52.63% win rate. Those four signals cannot all be right and picking one is a judgement call, not a fact I can source.
